<section class="section">
  <div class="section-kicker">Prospective researchers</div>
  <h2>Working with me</h2>
  <div class="section-copy">
    <p>I am particularly interested in supervising work on the cognitive representation of meaning and in projects that bring linguistic theory into conversation with experimental psycholinguistics.</p>
    <p>Good fits could involve linguistic representation, incremental interpretation, inference and prediction, memory and knowledge, discourse, or related questions at the interface of language and cognition.</p>
    <div class="callout"><strong>Application note.</strong> The exact opportunities and funding routes change over time. Prospective researchers should use the contact details below to ask about current supervision possibilities and fit.</div>
    <p><a href="mailto:matthew.husband@ling-phil.ox.ac.uk">Email me about research fit →</a></p>
  </div>
</section>

  <h2>Oxford</h2>
  <p class="section-copy">I am Professor of Psycholinguistics in the Faculty of Linguistics, Philology and Phonetics at the University of Oxford and a Tutorial Fellow at St Hugh's College. My research is carried out within Oxford's psycholinguistics research community.</p>
